title: Barge Hull Gauging Training for Gulf Coast Brown-Water Fleets
description: Gulf Coast maritime NDT training for barge fleets on Subchapter M, class tonnage under ESP, and Mobile/Pascagoula new build. On-site cohorts, no crew travel.
h1: Hull Gauging and Weld NDT Training Built Around Gulf Coast Drydock Windows
answer: Gulf Coast maritime NDT training splits three ways: inland barge fleets on Subchapter M drydock and internal structural exams, offshore service vessels under class survey, and new construction at Mobile and Pascagoula. Atlantis delivers cohort training at the yard or operator's facility so crews qualify without leaving the region during turnaround season.
expansion: The Gulf Coast is not one maritime market. Kirby Inland Marine alone runs 1,134 tank barges and 291 towboats across the Mississippi River System, the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and the Houston Ship Channel, and those hulls are inspected under 46 CFR Subchapter M rather than class rules — a drydock and internal structural exam once in five years for freshwater service, twice in five years for vessels in salt water more than six months of any twelve. Blue-water tonnage calling at Houston, Mobile and Pascagoula runs the Enhanced Survey Programme instead, with close-up survey and thickness measurement scope widening as the hull ages. New construction at Austal USA in Mobile and Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding in Pascagoula adds a third regime again — weld inspection to build specification under NAVSEA technical publications. A Gulf Coast technician who knows only one of the three is employable in one lane.

facets.q: How often must a Gulf Coast towing vessel be drydocked for hull examination?
facets.a: 46 CFR part 137 subpart C requires a drydock and internal structural examination at least once in five years for a towing vessel not exposed to salt water more than six months in any twelve-month period. A vessel that does exceed that exposure needs the examination twice in five years, with no more than 36 months between them. Freshwater Lower Mississippi barges sit in the first band; Gulf and coastal units sit in the second.

facets.q: Does a class drydock survey satisfy the Subchapter M requirement?
facets.a: Yes. Coast Guard guidance confirms that a drydock and internal structural examination performed for a towing vessel to maintain a valid load line certificate, or to maintain class with the American Bureau of Shipping or another recognized classification society in accordance with their rules, counts as an examination required under 46 CFR 137.300. Operators running mixed class and Subchapter M fleets use that credit deliberately to consolidate dockings and gauging campaigns.

facets.q: What NDT certification does a barge hull gauging technician need?
facets.a: Ultrasonic Level II is the working requirement. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice, equipment setup, interpretation of results and reporting are Level II functions, and Level II in ultrasonics carries 80 hours of training in total plus several hundred hours of documented method experience scaled by prior education. Certification is issued by the employer against the employer's written practice, not by a training vendor, which is a distinction Gulf operators are audited on.

facets.q: Why do Gulf Coast operators insist on on-site cohort training?
facets.a: Turnaround season removes the option of sending people away. Refinery and terminal turnarounds commit every certified inspector in the region to fixed windows, and the barge and workboat operators feeding those terminals cannot release crews either. Sending one technician to an out-of-state open-enrolment course costs billable time, travel and schedule risk. Moving the instructor instead keeps the crew inside the region and puts the practical stations on the company's own instruments and specimens.

facets.q: What changes when the work is at Austal USA or Ingalls instead of a barge yard?
facets.a: The governing document changes. Navy and Coast Guard construction runs on NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, which requires the employer to hold a written practice meeting SNT-TC-1A as modified by that publication. The modifications include a three-year certification interval instead of five, mandatory technical performance evaluations, and recertification by examination at every level including Level III. A commercial marine Level II certificate does not transfer into that system without recertification.

facets.q: Which Gulf ports and yards does Atlantis run maritime cohorts for?
facets.a: Cohorts run across the Houston Ship Channel and Galveston Bay corridor, including Channelview, Brady Island and Galveston, into the Louisiana inland market around Lockport, Morgan City and the Lower Mississippi fleeting areas, and east to Mobile and Pascagoula. Delivery is at the operator's facility or the yard's own training room. Demo and cohort scheduling is quoted on request through the contact page, built around the employer's docking and certification expiry calendar.

sections.heading: The Gulf Coast Is Three Training Markets Wearing One Name
paragraphs: The stretch from Brownsville to Pensacola carries the densest concentration of marine repair capacity in the United States, and the vessels inside it answer to three different inspection authorities. Inland tank barges and towboats fall under 46 CFR Subchapter M, enforced by the Coast Guard through drydock and internal structural examinations. Foreign-going tankers and bulk carriers calling Houston, Texas City and Mobile fall under the Enhanced Survey Programme and their classification society's rules. Navy and Coast Guard hulls under construction at Mobile and Pascagoula answer to NAVSEA technical publications instead.

A technician certified for one is not automatically credible in the next. The methods overlap heavily — ultrasonic thickness gauging, magnetic particle on repair welds, visual on structural fit-up — but the qualification paperwork, the acceptance criteria and the report format do not. Gulf Coast cohort training that names all three regimes explicitly produces a technician who knows which rulebook governs the hull in front of them, and which certificate their employer has to be able to produce when the surveyor or the government quality assurance representative asks for it.

sections.heading: Subchapter M Sets the Calendar for the Brown-Water Fleet
paragraphs: 46 CFR part 137 subpart C requires every towing vessel to undergo a drydock and internal structural examination at least once in five years when the vessel is not exposed to salt water more than six months in any twelve-month period. Vessels that do exceed that salt-water exposure need the examination twice in five years, with no more than 36 months between them. A drydock examination performed to maintain load line, or to maintain class with ABS or another recognized organization under their rules, counts toward the Subchapter M requirement.

That structure produces a predictable, rolling demand for hull gauging across the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and the Lower Mississippi. Kirby Inland Marine alone operates 1,134 tank barges and 291 towboats across the Mississippi River System, the GIWW and the Houston Ship Channel — roughly 27 percent of a national inland tank barge fleet of about 4,000 units. Every one of those hulls reaches an examination date, and every examination date creates a gauging scope that somebody certified has to execute and report.

Coast Guard guidance points to NVIC 7-68 for the minimum hull thickness gauging pattern on an existing vessel. Technicians who learn gauging as nothing more than putting a probe down and reading a number fail at that point: the work is a mapped pattern with recorded locations, original thickness, measured thickness and a wastage calculation against an allowance. The [training hours breakdown by method](/blog/ndt-training-hours-requirements-by-method) sets out the ultrasonic classroom and practical minimums that stand behind the skill.

sections.heading: Houston Ship Channel and Galveston Bay: Where the Capacity Sits
paragraphs: Southwest Shipyard operates four facilities along the Texas Gulf Coast — Channelview, Brady Island, Brady Island West and Galveston — and ranks among the largest shipyard and barge cleaning operations on the coast, all with deep-water access to the Gulf. Bludworth Marine's Galveston yard on Harborside Drive handles offshore construction and supply vessels alongside inland tugs and barges, with graving docks sized for mid-draft hulls. Taylor Marine Construction has built a new haul-out facility on Dickinson Bayou immediately adjacent to the ship channel, placing a 660-ton Marine Travelift into commercial service in August 2026.

That concentration matters for training logistics more than for anything else. A cohort assembled in Channelview draws technicians who can be back on a barge the same afternoon, and that is the only arrangement most Gulf operators will accept during a working quarter. The [Houston maritime NDT consulting](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting-houston) practice runs the procedure and written-practice side of the same engagements, so the classroom content and the yard's controlling documents state the same acceptance criteria and the same reporting format.

sections.heading: Louisiana Inland: Lockport, Morgan City and the Lower Mississippi
paragraphs: Bollinger Shipyards, headquartered at Lockport, runs shipyards along the Gulf of Mexico across southern Louisiana and Texas, with drydocks up to 10,500 tons serving shallow-draft and deepwater vessels alike. Its legacy is inland waterway pushboats and ocean-going double hull barges, which places it in the middle of the Lower Mississippi repair market. Fleeting areas between Baton Rouge and the Head of Passes hold barges waiting on shipyard slots, and a large share of the gauging work happens at the fleet rather than on a dock floor.

Training in Louisiana therefore has to cover in-service gauging conditions: coated plate, marine growth, pitted internals, and access restricted to a barge deck. A technician trained only on machined calibration blocks reads a corroded rake tank bottom wrong. Practical stations built for this market mirror the actual surface condition of a fifteen-year-old hopper or tank barge, and put couplant selection, transducer choice and the echo-to-echo decision in the trainee's hands before any sign-off happens.

The reporting side carries equal weight. A gauging report that a Coast Guard marine inspector or an attending class surveyor rejects for pattern coverage or missing original-thickness data sends the vessel back for re-gauging, and on the Lower Mississippi that means another fleeting move. Reporting discipline is taught as an examinable skill in its own right rather than as a closing remark on the final day of a course.

sections.heading: Mobile and Pascagoula: New Construction Changes the Standard
paragraphs: Ingalls Shipbuilding at Pascagoula employs more than 11,000 people. Austal USA in Mobile employs over 3,000, ranks as the world's leading aluminium shipbuilder, and is spending $288 million on expansion, with a new surface ship assembly building of more than 192,000 square feet due for completion in early 2027 to build the Coast Guard's Offshore Patrol Cutter and the Navy's TAGOS-25 ocean surveillance ships. Bollinger acquired VT Halter Marine at Pascagoula in November 2022, renaming it Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding and taking over the Polar Security Cutter programme.

Government construction pulls the qualification standard away from commercial marine practice. NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 sets requirements for radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual inspection on Navy work, and requires the employer to hold a written practice meeting SNT-TC-1A as modified by the publication. Those modifications include a three-year certification interval, technical performance evaluations, and recertification by examination at every level, Level III included.

Mobile carries a documented skills shortage on the welding side: regional training programmes produce 60 to 70 qualified aluminium welders a year against demand for 150 or more. Inspection capacity tracks welding capacity, and a yard that cannot inspect at rate cannot weld at rate. [Corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) programmes are built for exactly that constraint — a defined cohort, a defined start date, and a certification outcome the yard's quality manager agreed to before day one.

sections.heading: Why Gulf Contractors Train Cohorts On Site
paragraphs: Turnaround season removes the option of sending people away. Refinery and terminal turnarounds pull inspection contractors into fixed windows where every certified body is committed, and the barge and workboat operators feeding those terminals cannot spare crews either. A four-week open-enrolment course in another state costs a Gulf contractor the technician's billable time, plus travel, plus the risk that the course schedule slips into a docking date the operator has already paid for.

On-site cohort delivery fixes the arithmetic. Instructors travel instead of students, the practical stations use the company's own instruments and the company's own hull specimens, and the examination happens in the same building on the same week. The employer's written practice governs the certification, which is how ASNT SNT-TC-1A intends it to work — the certificate is issued by the employer, not by a training vendor. [Written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) closes that loop where the employer's document is thin or out of date.

sections.heading: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging Is the Bottleneck Skill
paragraphs: Every Gulf maritime regime lands on the same measurement. Subchapter M gaugings, class renewal survey thickness measurement, and new-construction plate verification all use pulse-echo ultrasonics on steel; what separates them is the reporting standard and the acceptance criteria rather than the physics. Level II is where the responsibility sits. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice, equipment setup, interpretation of results and reporting are Level II functions, and ultrasonic Level II carries 80 hours of training with several hundred hours of documented method experience behind it.

On class-committed tonnage the operator also has to sit inside an approved supplier's system. IACS UR Z17 governs approval of firms providing statutory and classification services including thickness measurement, requires certification to the current ISO 9000 series, and results in a certificate of approval that states the type and scope of services along with any limitations or restrictions imposed. [UTM operator qualification and class approval](/consulting/utm-operator-qualification-class-approval) covers that pathway from the operator's side, and [IACS service supplier approval](/consulting/iacs-service-supplier-approval) covers the audit itself.

The pay signal follows the qualification. Published salary data for [NDT Level II technicians](/ndt-level-2-salary) puts marine and offshore gauging work at the upper end of the Level II band, because the schedule pressure is real and the certified population on the Gulf is small relative to the number of hulls reaching an examination date. For an operator that is an argument to train from inside: a deckhand or a welder who already understands barge structure becomes a gauging technician faster than an outside hire learns the fleet.

sections.heading: Offshore Service Vessels and the Class Overlay
paragraphs: The offshore supply, crew and construction fleet working out of Port Fourchon, Galveston, Sabine and Cameron adds a fourth pattern. These vessels sit in salt water year-round, which places them in the twice-in-five-years drydock band, and most carry classification on top of Coast Guard certification. The NDT scope widens past hull gauging into magnetic particle on crane pedestals, A-frames and towing gear foundations, and penetrant testing on aluminium superstructure and deck fittings.

That belongs in the curriculum as a distinct module rather than an afterthought, because the acceptance criteria come from a different document and the geometry is unfamiliar to a technician trained on flat plate. [Offshore NDT consulting](/consulting/offshore-ndt-consulting) supplies the procedures; the training supplies the hands and the examinable proficiency. Contractors running crews in both the inland and offshore markets get one cohort that leaves qualified for both, which is the only way to staff a fleet that moves between the two on short notice.

sections.heading: How the Gulf Programme Connects to the Rest of the US Coastline
paragraphs: A Gulf-qualified technician travels well. The same ultrasonic Level II certificate that supports a Subchapter M gauging scope in Channelview supports commercial class work in Norfolk or ferry hull gauging in Seattle, and the regional difference is the survey regime rather than the method. The [Hampton Roads programme](/training/maritime-ndt-training-hampton-roads) covers the NAVSEA-versus-IACS split that defines the Virginia market, and the [Pacific Northwest programme](/training/maritime-ndt-training-pacific-northwest) covers the single seasonal window that defines Puget Sound.

For companies operating in more than one region, the practical answer is one written practice, one procedure set and one training standard applied at three locations. Keeping those documents identical means a technician transferred from Houston to Norfolk does not restart the qualification clock, and an auditor reviewing the Gulf operation sees the same controlling document the Virginia operation runs on. Cohort scheduling and a written-practice review are quoted on request through [contact](/contact).

faq.q: Do Gulf Coast barge operators need class approval to gauge their own hulls?
faq.a: No, when the gauging supports a Subchapter M drydock and internal structural examination for the operator's own fleet. Class service supplier approval under IACS UR Z17 applies where thickness measurement results are used by a class surveyor to make decisions affecting classification. Operators whose barges also carry class, or who gauge for third parties, need the approval and the certified-operator records behind it.

faq.q: Can Atlantis run a cohort at our fleeting area rather than a shipyard?
faq.a: Yes. Instructors travel to the operator's facility, whether that is a fleeting area office, a barge cleaning yard, a fabrication shop or a corporate training room. Practical stations use the company's own instruments and hull specimens so the technical performance evaluation assesses the equipment the technician will actually use. Scheduling is built around docking dates and existing certification expiries rather than a public course calendar.

faq.q: Does Atlantis provide API 510, 570 or 653 inspector training?
faq.a: No. Those certifications sit with API and its authorised training providers, and Atlantis does not deliver them. Atlantis training covers NDT method qualification under ASNT SNT-TC-1A and employer written practices, including ultrasonic, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual, eddy current and radiographic methods, plus the maritime survey context those methods are used in. Fixed-equipment inspector certification is a separate pathway.

faq.q: What does the Enhanced Survey Programme require that Subchapter M does not?
faq.a: The 2011 ESP Code applies to self-propelled bulk carriers of 500 gross tonnage and above and to oil tankers, and prescribes the minimum extent of examination, thickness measurement and tank testing at annual, intermediate and renewal surveys. It requires close-up survey of specified structural elements and a thickness measurement report giving location, measured thickness and corresponding original thickness. Subchapter M sets an examination interval without that prescribed structural scope.

faq.q: How far in advance should we schedule a Gulf Coast cohort?
faq.a: Work backwards from the first certification expiry or docking date in the window. A UT Level II built from a standing start is a multi-month commitment because of the documented method experience requirement; a Level I upgrading to Level II is materially shorter. Booking during the quarter before turnaround season keeps instructors available and keeps the cohort out of the period when every certified technician in the region is committed.

faq.q: Who issues the certificate at the end of the cohort?
faq.a: The employer does. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and under NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for government work, certification is granted by the employer against the employer's written practice. The training provider supplies instruction, examination material and Level III oversight. Where a company has no Level III of record, [ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) supplies one so the certificates issued hold up on audit.

title: Tech Pub 271 and IACS Dual-Track NDT Training in Hampton Roads
description: Hampton Roads NDT training for both lanes: NAVSEA Tech Pub 271 qualification for Navy contract work and IACS class rules for commercial ship repair in Norfolk.
h1: Qualifying NDT Technicians for Navy Contract and Class Work in Norfolk
answer: Hampton Roads runs two NDT rulebooks side by side. Navy contract work qualifies technicians under NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, which modifies SNT-TC-1A with a three-year certification interval and recertification by examination at every level. Commercial class work runs on IACS unified requirements and service supplier approval. Atlantis trains Norfolk cohorts for both lanes inside the yard.
expansion: Virginia's shipyards employ more than 33,500 people, and the yards that matter for NDT sit within a few miles of each other on the Elizabeth River and Hampton Roads harbour. Norfolk Naval Shipyard at Portsmouth, General Dynamics NASSCO-Norfolk on Ligon Street, BAE Systems Norfolk Ship Repair, Colonna's Shipyard, Lyon Shipyard, East Coast Repair & Fabrication, Fairlead Boatworks and MHI Ship Repair all draw from one labour pool, with Newport News Shipbuilding and its roughly 25,000 employees across the water. Density is not what defines the market, though. The split does. A carrier availability at Portsmouth and a bulk carrier renewal survey at a commercial pier both call for ultrasonic and magnetic particle inspection, and the two jobs qualify the technician under entirely separate documents with different recertification clocks. Hampton Roads hiring managers screen on which of the two you hold, and dual qualification is the local advantage.

facets.q: What NDT standard governs Navy contract work in Hampton Roads?
facets.a: NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, Requirements for Nondestructive Testing Methods. It covers radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual inspection, and sets the minimum requirements to qualify NDT personnel, procedures and equipment. It requires the employer to hold a written practice meeting ASNT SNT-TC-1A as modified by the publication, which makes SNT-TC-1A the floor rather than the finished requirement.

facets.q: How does Tech Pub 271 differ from plain SNT-TC-1A?
facets.a: Three modifications matter most. The certification interval is three years rather than the five years SNT-TC-1A recommends. Technical performance evaluations are mandatory — an observed, documented demonstration of method proficiency rather than a written examination alone. And recertification is by examination at every level, Level III included, which removes the credit-based renewal route many technicians rely on in commercial industrial work.

facets.q: Can one technician be qualified for both Navy and commercial class work?
facets.a: Yes, and in Hampton Roads it is the strongest position to hold. The method core is shared: the same instrument, transducer selection logic and couplant discipline apply on a Navy hull and a commercial bulk carrier. What differs is the governing written practice, the acceptance criteria, the report format and the recertification clock. A single cohort can carry a common method core with two documented compliance branches.

facets.q: What does IACS UR Z17 require of a thickness measurement firm in Norfolk?
facets.a: UR Z17 sets the procedural requirements for approval of service suppliers providing statutory and classification services, thickness measurement included. The supplier must be certified to the current ISO 9000 series and demonstrate the competence and control needed for the services sought. The society issues a certificate of approval stating the type and scope of services and any limitations or restrictions imposed, including equipment type where that is a limiting constraint.

facets.q: Which Hampton Roads yards run mixed Navy and commercial workloads?
facets.a: Colonna's Shipyard is the clearest example — founded in 1875, the oldest continuously operating family-owned shipyard in the United States, 120 acres in Norfolk with about 750 employees and a $79 million fourth drydock of roughly 25,000 tons lifting capacity. Lyon Shipyard and East Coast Repair & Fabrication carry mixed workloads as well. Those yards are where dual qualification stops being optional and becomes a staffing requirement.

facets.q: Why is Hampton Roads NDT training delivered inside the yard?
facets.a: Access control decides it. Navy work requires badging, and moving a cohort in and out of a controlled facility for an external course burns days the availability schedule does not have. Delivering instruction on site removes the movement, and the practical stations use the yard's own instruments, specimens and procedures — which is what a technical performance evaluation under Tech Pub 271 is supposed to assess in the first place.

sections.heading: Two Rulebooks in One Harbour
paragraphs: Hampton Roads holds the densest ship repair market in the United States. Virginia's shipyards employ more than 33,500 workers and operate dry docks, mobile repair teams and the country's largest mobile boat hoist. The yards that matter for NDT sit within a few miles of each other: Norfolk Naval Shipyard at Portsmouth, BAE Systems Norfolk Ship Repair, Colonna's Shipyard, General Dynamics NASSCO-Norfolk, Lyon Shipyard, East Coast Repair & Fabrication, Fairlead Boatworks and MHI Ship Repair, with Newport News Shipbuilding across the water.

Density is not what defines the market. The split does. A carrier availability at Portsmouth and a bulk carrier renewal survey at a commercial pier both need ultrasonic and magnetic particle inspection, and the two jobs qualify the technician under entirely separate documents. One runs on NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271. The other runs on IACS unified requirements and the classification society's service supplier approval. Norfolk hiring managers screen candidates on which of the two they hold, and the technicians who hold both work continuously.

sections.heading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard and the Public Yard Standard
paragraphs: Norfolk Naval Shipyard at Portsmouth builds, repairs, overhauls and modernises Navy ships and submarines, and ranks among the largest employers in the Hampton Roads region. Work inside a public yard runs on the government's own technical publications, and NDT is no exception. T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 covers radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual inspection, and states the minimum requirements necessary to qualify NDT personnel, procedures and equipment for determining the presence of discontinuities in metals.

The publication does not replace SNT-TC-1A. It requires the employer to hold a written practice that meets SNT-TC-1A as modified by the publication, which makes SNT-TC-1A the floor and 271 the ceiling. That distinction catches technicians who arrive from refinery, pipeline or fabrication work holding a perfectly valid Level II and discover the certificate does not satisfy the naval written practice. [NAVSEA NDT requirements guidance for shipyards](/consulting/navsea-ndt-requirements-shipyard) sets out the gap in full and what the employer's document has to contain to close it.

sections.heading: The Master Ship Repair Yards
paragraphs: General Dynamics NASSCO-Norfolk is the consolidation of two long-standing Hampton Roads yards, the former Metro Machine Corporation and the former Earl Industries, both of which operated in the Port of Hampton Roads for more than fifty years. Metro Machine was founded in 1963, won its first Master Ship Repair Agreement with the Navy in 1966, moved to the Ligon Street yard in 1971 and was acquired by NASSCO in 2011. Ligon Street operates three piers, a 40,000 long ton drydock able to dock LHD-1 and LHA-6 class ships, and five tower cranes.

Colonna's Shipyard, established in 1875 by Charles J. Colonna, is the oldest continuously operating family-owned shipyard in the United States and is now led by the fifth generation of the family. It covers 120 acres in Norfolk with roughly 750 employees, and has committed $79 million to a fourth drydock of approximately 25,000 tons lifting capacity, 147 feet wide and 725 feet long. Yards with that profile carry Navy and commercial work simultaneously, which is the exact condition that forces dual qualification on the inspection staff.

MHI Ship Repair & Services now sits under Vigor Marine Group, which unified five marine industrial companies and operates facilities in Seattle, Portland, Vancouver Washington, San Diego and Norfolk. That corporate structure links the Hampton Roads and Puget Sound labour markets directly. A technician certified against a group-wide written practice is deployable across both coasts without a fresh qualification cycle, which is a real advantage when availability schedules move.

sections.heading: Newport News Shipbuilding and the Construction Side
paragraphs: HII's Newport News Shipbuilding employs roughly 25,000 people and stands as the largest industrial employer in Virginia and the largest private employer in Hampton Roads. Construction work, as opposed to repair, generates a different NDT profile: volumetric inspection of new welds at high volume, radiography and ultrasonics on thick section material, and a documentation burden tied to a build specification rather than to a survey credit. The certification pathway is still the 271-modified written practice, but the daily work looks nothing like a hull gauging scope.

For the surrounding supplier base — fabricators, machine shops and subcontract inspection houses feeding the yard — the requirement is qualifying people against the prime contractor's flowed-down requirements. Training that stops at the SNT-TC-1A syllabus leaves the supplier short at the first quality audit. [Corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) engagements start by reading the flow-down, then build the cohort around it, so the certification the technician walks out with is the one the prime's quality organisation accepts.

sections.heading: What Tech Pub 271 Changes About Your Certificate
paragraphs: Three modifications carry the weight. First, the certification interval is three years rather than the five years SNT-TC-1A recommends, which compresses the recertification cycle and turns training into a recurring cost rather than a one-off project. Second, technical performance evaluations are required — a documented, observed demonstration of method proficiency, not a written examination alone. Third, recertification is by examination at every level, Level III included, which removes the credit-based renewal route many technicians rely on in commercial industrial work.

The practical consequence for a Norfolk employer is a permanently live training calendar. A shop with forty certified technicians on three-year intervals recertifies more than one a month on average, and each recertification consumes instructor time, specimens and examination administration. Building that into an annual plan costs less than reacting to expiries discovered during an availability. Hampton Roads cohorts scheduled against the employer's expiry list rather than a public calendar keep the certified headcount flat instead of sawtoothed.

sections.heading: The Commercial Class Lane
paragraphs: Commercial tonnage in Hampton Roads answers to its classification society instead. Thickness measurement whose results a class surveyor uses to make decisions affecting classification has to come from an approved service supplier, and IACS UR Z17 sets the procedural requirements for that approval: certification to the current ISO 9000 series, demonstrated competence and control over the services performed, and a certificate of approval stating the type and scope of services along with any limitations or restrictions imposed, including equipment type where that is a limiting constraint.

Operators listed under that approval need ultrasonic qualification at Level II, because equipment setup, interpretation of results and reporting are Level II responsibilities under SNT-TC-1A. The certificate alone is not sufficient — the individual has to sit inside the approved firm's system with training and experience records an auditor can inspect. [UTM operator qualification and class approval](/consulting/utm-operator-qualification-class-approval) builds those records, and [IACS service supplier approval](/consulting/iacs-service-supplier-approval) covers the audit and the certificate scope itself.

sections.heading: Dual-Qualifying a Hampton Roads Technician
paragraphs: The two lanes overlap far more in method than in paperwork. A technician performing ultrasonic thickness measurement on a Navy hull and on a commercial bulk carrier uses the same instrument, the same transducer selection logic and the same couplant discipline. What differs is the governing written practice, the acceptance criteria, the report format and the recertification clock. Training both inside a single cohort is efficient precisely because the physics and the hand skill are shared across the divide.

The Norfolk curriculum is built as a common method core with two compliance branches. The core covers ultrasonic theory, calibration, corrosion mapping, weld inspection and reporting. Branch one maps the work onto the 271-modified written practice, the technical performance evaluation and the three-year clock. Branch two maps it onto class survey scope, UR Z17 supplier records and what the attending surveyor expects at a renewal survey. A technician finishes holding one certification with two documented scopes.

That structure also protects the employer through a workload swing. When Navy availabilities compress and commercial repair picks up, or the reverse, a dual-qualified crew moves without a fresh qualification cycle and without a gap in coverage. [Maritime NDT consulting in Norfolk](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting-norfolk) keeps the two branches of the written practice aligned as NAVSEA standard items and class rules are revised, so the document does not drift between audit cycles.

sections.heading: Why the Training Happens Inside the Yard
paragraphs: Access control decides the logistics. Navy work requires badging, and moving a cohort of technicians in and out of a controlled facility for a public course consumes days the availability schedule does not have. Delivering instruction inside the yard removes the movement entirely, and the practical stations use the yard's own instruments, specimens and procedures — which is what the technical performance evaluation is meant to assess anyway, rather than proficiency on a training-room instrument the technician will never see again.

The examination follows the same logic. Certification under SNT-TC-1A, and under Tech Pub 271 for government work, is issued by the employer against the employer's written practice. A training provider supplies instruction, examination material and Level III oversight; the employer supplies the certificate and owns it. Where the written practice is out of date or was written for a different scope, [written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) rewrites it before the cohort runs so the certificates issued survive the next audit.

sections.heading: How Norfolk Connects to the Other US Maritime Markets
paragraphs: A technician who understands the NAVSEA-versus-class split in Hampton Roads holds the most portable maritime qualification in the country. The [Gulf Coast programme](/training/maritime-ndt-training-gulf-coast) adds Subchapter M barge and workboat gauging plus new construction at Mobile and Pascagoula, and the [Pacific Northwest programme](/training/maritime-ndt-training-pacific-northwest) adds ferry and fishing fleet work compressed into a single seasonal window. The method core is identical across all three; only the rulebook and the calendar change.

For contractors bidding nationally, one written practice covering NAVSEA, class and Coast Guard scopes is the asset that wins the work. [ASNT certification guidance](/asnt-certification) explains what employer-based certification commits a company to, and [ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) supplies the Level III of record where a company does not employ one directly. A Hampton Roads cohort schedule and a written-practice review are quoted on request through [contact](/contact).

faq.q: Does my existing ASNT Level II certificate work at a Norfolk Navy repair yard?
faq.a: Not by itself. Certification under both SNT-TC-1A and Tech Pub 271 is issued by the employer against the employer's written practice, so a certificate from a previous employer does not transfer. The new employer evaluates prior training and experience, then certifies against its own document. Prior Level II training and documented method hours shorten the pathway substantially, but the certificate itself is reissued.

faq.q: What is a technical performance evaluation and why does Tech Pub 271 require one?
faq.a: It is a documented, observed demonstration that the technician can perform the method to the written practice — set up the equipment, calibrate it, run the examination and report the result correctly. Tech Pub 271 mandates it because a written examination alone does not prove hand skill on a naval structure. Practical stations in a yard cohort are built to produce exactly that evidence for the certification file.

faq.q: Does Atlantis deliver API 510, 570 or 653 inspector training in Hampton Roads?
faq.a: No. Those certifications belong to API and its authorised providers, and Atlantis does not deliver them. Atlantis covers NDT method qualification under ASNT SNT-TC-1A and employer written practices, including the NAVSEA Tech Pub 271 modifications for government work and the class survey context for commercial work. Fixed-equipment inspector certification is a separate pathway from NDT method certification.

faq.q: How long does it take to dual-qualify an existing Level II for the Navy lane?
faq.a: For a technician already holding documented ultrasonic training and method experience, the work is the 271-specific delta: the modified written practice content, the technical performance evaluation, and examination under the new employer's document. That is measured in days rather than months. Building a Level II from a standing start is a multi-month commitment because of the documented method experience requirement behind the certification.

faq.q: Can a commercial thickness measurement crew support a class renewal survey without supplier approval?
faq.a: No, where the results will be used by the class surveyor to make decisions affecting classification. IACS UR Z17 requires the firm to hold a certificate of approval from the society, certified to the current ISO 9000 series, with the scope and any limitations stated on the certificate. The individual operators must be inside that approved system with inspectable training and experience records.

faq.q: When should we schedule a Hampton Roads cohort?
faq.a: Schedule against the certification expiry list, not the calendar. With a three-year interval under Tech Pub 271, a shop of forty certified technicians has recertifications falling every month. Grouping them into two or three cohorts a year, placed between availabilities, keeps instructor cost down and keeps the certified headcount stable. A written-practice review before the first cohort prevents reissuing certificates against an outdated document.

title: Puget Sound Winter Layup NDT Training for Ferry and Trawler Fleets
description: Puget Sound NDT training scheduled around one maintenance window: Washington State Ferries layups, the Alaska fleet's January deadline, and Bremerton work.
h1: NDT Training Timed to the Pacific Northwest's One Maintenance Window
answer: Pacific Northwest maritime NDT training runs on a deadline, not a calendar. Washington State Ferries needs 19 of its 21 vessels for summer service, and the Bering Sea pollock A season opens 20 January. Every gauging technician working those hulls has to be certified before the yards fill in October. Atlantis trains Puget Sound cohorts in the shoulder season.
expansion: Puget Sound maintenance is not spread evenly across the year. Washington State Ferries operates the largest ferry fleet in the country — 21 auto-passenger vessels on eight routes between twenty terminals — and full service needs 19 of them in summer, 18 in the shoulder seasons and 17 in winter, against a system that reliably operates 17 or 18. Eleven of those vessels are more than forty years old and one is sixty-seven. Meanwhile the North Pacific fishing fleet homeported at Terminal 91 and Fishermen's Terminal comes off the water when pollock season winds down at the end of October, runs maintenance through Seattle in late November, and has to be back in Alaskan waters before the Bering Sea A season opens on 20 January. Both fleets compete for a documented shortage of drydock space in western Washington. Inspection capacity has to exist before that window opens, not during it.

Drydock capacity in western Washington is documented by WSF as limited and difficult to secure on short notice, which is what turns an inspection delay into a service reduction.

facets.q: Why is Pacific Northwest NDT training seasonal?
facets.a: Because the vessels are. Washington State Ferries needs 19 of 21 vessels in service for summer, and the North Pacific fishing fleet has to sail before 20 January. Both fleets are alongside during the same narrow autumn and winter months, and both draw on the same limited drydock capacity in western Washington. A technician whose certification lapses in November is unusable in December, when the entire year's inspection work lands.

facets.q: When does the Alaska fleet's maintenance window close?
facets.a: Effectively in early January. The pollock season winds down at the end of October, the trawlers and factory processors return to Terminal 91 and Fishermen's Terminal, and maintenance and upgrade work runs through Seattle in late November. By January the fleet is back in Alaskan waters. The Bering Sea pollock A season opens 20 January and runs to 10 June, and a vessel that misses it does not get a second window.

facets.q: How many vessels does Washington State Ferries need in service?
facets.a: Full service on every route needs 19 vessels in summer, 18 in the spring and autumn shoulder seasons, and 17 in late autumn, winter and early spring. The system currently operates 17 or 18 reliably out of a fleet of 21. The fleet has fallen from 25 vessels in 2015 to 21 in 2025 through retirements, so there is no spare hull to absorb an inspection finding that extends a docking.

facets.q: What NDT scope does a ferry hull preservation docking generate?
facets.a: Ultrasonic thickness gauging of shell and deck plate dominates, and the scope is heavier than on a young hull because eleven WSF vessels are more than forty years old and one is sixty-seven. Magnetic particle and penetrant testing cover rudder stocks, shaft components and structural renewals, with visual inspection of coatings and internal structure alongside. Wastage on a forty-year-old shell plate is a structural finding, not a data point.

facets.q: What standard applies at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard?
facets.a: NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271. It covers radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual inspection and sets the minimum requirements to qualify NDT personnel, procedures and equipment. The employer must hold a written practice meeting SNT-TC-1A as modified by the publication, which brings a three-year certification interval, mandatory technical performance evaluations and recertification by examination at every level including Level III.

facets.q: When should a Puget Sound contractor start a training cohort?
facets.a: Spring through late summer, while the ferries are in service and the fishing fleet is north. That is the only period when technicians are releasable, instructors are available and examinations can be completed without competing against a docking. Working backwards from an October readiness date, a Level II built from a standing start needs the spring; a Level I upgrading to Level II needs materially less.

sections.heading: The Region Runs on One Window
paragraphs: Puget Sound maritime maintenance is not spread evenly across the year. The Washington State Ferries fleet has to be at maximum availability for the summer, the North Pacific fishing fleet has to be at sea in January, and both draw on the same limited pool of drydock space in western Washington. Everything that has to be inspected gets inspected in the months when the vessels are alongside, and the window closes on a date that no operator, yard or inspection contractor controls.

That reshapes what training means here. A Gulf Coast operator schedules gauging around a rolling five-year examination cycle and absorbs slippage. A Puget Sound operator schedules it against a fixed calendar deadline, and a technician whose certification lapses in November is worthless in December. Training in this region has to complete before the window opens, not during it, which makes the cohort a spring and summer decision rather than an autumn one.

sections.heading: Washington State Ferries: 21 Vessels, No Spare
paragraphs: Washington State Ferries operates the largest ferry fleet in the country — 21 auto-passenger vessels running eight routes between twenty terminals across Puget Sound and the San Juan Islands. Operating full service on every route requires 19 vessels in summer, 18 in the spring and autumn shoulder seasons and 17 in late autumn, winter and early spring. The system currently operates 17 or 18 reliably, depending on the season. There is no float in that arithmetic.

The fleet is also old. Eleven vessels are more than forty years old, one of them sixty-seven, and the fleet has shrunk from 25 vessels in 2015 to 21 in 2025 through retirements. Eastern Shipbuilding Group has begun construction on the first of three 160-vehicle hybrid-electric ferries after the state exercised its option for a third. Age drives gauging scope directly: wastage found on a forty-year-old shell plate is a structural finding with a repair attached, not a number in a table.

WSF has documented that drydock space in western Washington is limited and difficult to secure on short notice for emergency repairs. A vessel that enters dock with an unresolved thickness question occupies a slot another vessel needs. Getting the gauging right the first time is therefore a fleet availability issue rather than an inspection issue, which is why the qualification of the inspection crew gets scrutinised before the docking rather than after it.

sections.heading: The Alaska Fleet's Hard Deadline
paragraphs: The North Pacific fishing fleet has homeported in the Seattle area for more than a century, at Terminal 91 and Fishermen's Terminal. The pollock season winds down at the end of October, the trawlers and factory processors come home, and maintenance and upgrade work runs through Seattle in late November while the vessels are sprinkled across the Pacific Northwest and the Lake Washington Ship Canal. By January most of them are back in Alaskan waters fishing long nights and short days.

The date that governs everything is 20 January, when the Bering Sea pollock A season opens and runs through 10 June. A catcher-processor that is not ready on 20 January does not get a second window that year. Owners treat every NDT finding during that layup as schedule risk with a dollar value attached, and an inspection contractor who cannot mobilise a certified crew in November loses the account to one who can.

The work itself is demanding. Factory trawler hulls carry heavy ice-strengthening, trawl gear foundations take cyclic loading, and refrigeration and processing spaces keep steel in a wet, salt-laden environment year-round. Ultrasonic gauging, magnetic particle on gear foundations and weld toes, and penetrant testing on aluminium structure are all in scope, and the technician performs them in a crowded yard on a clock that does not move.

sections.heading: Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and the Bremerton Standard
paragraphs: Puget Sound Naval Shipyard at Bremerton has been in uninterrupted use since 1891 and employs around 15,000 people, making it the largest public shipyard in the United States by personnel assigned. Work there and across its surrounding supplier base runs on NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, which sets requirements for radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual inspection along with the minimum requirements to qualify NDT personnel, procedures and equipment.

The publication requires the employer to maintain a written practice meeting SNT-TC-1A as modified by 271: a three-year certification interval, mandatory technical performance evaluations, and recertification by examination at every level including Level III. A technician moving from commercial ferry work into Bremerton-adjacent work does not carry a certificate across; the new employer certifies against its own written practice. [NAVSEA NDT requirements guidance for shipyards](/consulting/navsea-ndt-requirements-shipyard) sets out precisely what that document has to contain.

sections.heading: Vigor and the Private Repair Capacity
paragraphs: Vigor Marine Group holds much of the region's commercial repair capacity, including a 27-acre facility on Seattle's Harbor Island for new construction and repair of mid-sized vessels, alongside yards at Portland, Vancouver Washington, San Diego and Norfolk. The group generated close to $1 billion in revenue in 2024 with roughly 2,700 employees, and its Seattle waterfront operations have served Washington State Ferries and the United States Navy since 1960 under successive owners.

In February 2026 Antin Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire Vigor Marine Group from an affiliate of Lone Star Funds, with the transaction expected to close during 2026. Ownership changes do not move the survey calendar. The ferries still have to be in service in June, the trawlers still have to sail on 20 January, and the inspection workforce still has to be qualified before either happens. Planning a cohort against the fleet calendar rather than the corporate one is the stable approach.

sections.heading: Drydock Scarcity Makes NDT a Scheduling Function
paragraphs: When dock slots are scarce, the cost of a late or disputed inspection result is measured in dock days rather than inspection hours. A thickness reading that a surveyor rejects for pattern coverage or reporting format sends the vessel back for re-gauging while the dock clock keeps running, and the next vessel in the queue slips with it. In a region operating 21 ferries with no spare hull, that consequence lands directly on the published sailing schedule.

The defence is procedural rather than technical. Gauging patterns agreed with the attending surveyor before the docking, reports formatted to the survey requirement with location, original thickness and measured thickness recorded, and technicians certified under a written practice the surveyor recognises together remove the failure mode. [Maritime NDT consulting in Seattle](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting-seattle) sets those procedures up; the training programme produces people who execute them the same way on every hull.

sections.heading: What the Seasonal Technician Must Hold Before October
paragraphs: Ultrasonic Level II is the gate. Equipment setup, interpretation of results and reporting are Level II functions under ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice, which places ultrasonic Level II at 80 hours of training in total with several hundred hours of documented method experience behind it, scaled by prior education. Visual and magnetic particle qualification accompany it in practice, because a hull docking scope rarely stops at plate thickness and the same technician handles the rudder, the shafting and the structural renewals.

The [hours-by-method breakdown](/blog/ndt-training-hours-requirements-by-method) sets out what each method costs in classroom and practical time, which is the input a Puget Sound employer needs in order to work backwards from an October readiness date. A Level II built from a standing start is a multi-month commitment. A Level I upgrading to Level II is considerably shorter. Planning the cohort in spring is what makes autumn readiness achievable rather than aspirational.

Third-party examination costs are real and worth budgeting separately. ASNT lists Level III examination fees between $365 and $1,105 for members and $440 to $1,780 for non-members depending on the exam, the location and the number of methods, with initial certification requiring both the Basic and a Method examination. ASNT has also confirmed that Basic examinations taken after 1 January 2026 reference the 2024 editions of SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 in place of the 2020 editions.

sections.heading: Training the Cohort in the Shoulder Season
paragraphs: The right time to run a Pacific Northwest cohort is spring through late summer, while the ferries are in service and the fishing fleet is north. Instructors travel to the operator's facility, practical stations use the company's own instruments and hull specimens, and examinations complete before the yards fill in the autumn. [Corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) programmes are scheduled against the employer's operational calendar rather than a public course list, which is the only arrangement that works in a single-window region.

Certification is issued by the employer against the employer's written practice, which is how SNT-TC-1A intends it to operate. Where an operator has no Level III of record, [ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) supplies one, and [written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) brings the controlling document current before the cohort runs. The certificate has to stand up in front of a class surveyor, a Coast Guard marine inspector or a government quality assurance representative, not merely in a personnel file.

sections.heading: The Same Technician Works Three Coasts
paragraphs: The methods do not change between Seattle, Norfolk and Houston. What changes is the survey regime and the calendar behind it. The [Hampton Roads programme](/training/maritime-ndt-training-hampton-roads) covers the NAVSEA-versus-IACS split that defines the Virginia market, and the [Gulf Coast programme](/training/maritime-ndt-training-gulf-coast) covers Subchapter M barge and workboat gauging alongside new construction at Mobile and Pascagoula. A technician who holds the method core can move between all three with a documentation delta rather than a fresh qualification.

For a Pacific Northwest contractor, that portability is a hedge against a thin season. A crew qualified for ferry hull gauging, Bremerton-adjacent government work and commercial class survey support has three demand curves instead of one, and the seasonal trough stops being idle time. The [national training footprint](/training-usa) and [ASNT certification guidance](/asnt-certification) exist to keep those qualifications aligned across regions. A Puget Sound cohort schedule is quoted on request through [contact](/contact).

faq.q: Can a cohort run during the autumn layup instead of the shoulder season?
faq.a: It runs badly. During the layup every technician is committed to a hull, dock slots are full and instructors compete with production for space and specimens. Certification that finishes in December arrives after the Alaska fleet has sailed and after the ferry preservation dockings are underway. Spring and summer delivery puts qualified people in place before the demand arrives, which is the entire point in a single-window region.

faq.q: Does Washington State Ferries work require class society qualification?
faq.a: WSF vessels operate under Coast Guard inspection rather than an IACS class survey regime, so service supplier approval under UR Z17 is not the governing requirement. Ultrasonic Level II under the employer's written practice, with documented method experience and a gauging pattern agreed with the attending inspector, is what carries the work. Contractors also serving foreign-going tonnage in the Sound need the class approval separately.

faq.q: Does Atlantis provide API 510, 570 or 653 inspector training in the Pacific Northwest?
faq.a: No. Those certifications belong to API and its authorised training providers, and Atlantis does not deliver them. Atlantis covers NDT method qualification under ASNT SNT-TC-1A and employer written practices — ultrasonic, magnetic particle, penetrant, visual, eddy current and radiographic — plus the survey and inspection context those methods serve in maritime work. Fixed-equipment inspector certification is a separate pathway.

faq.q: How does gauging an ice-strengthened trawler hull differ from a ferry hull?
faq.a: Plate thickness and structural arrangement change the technique. Ice-strengthened shell plate is thicker and more heavily framed, which alters transducer selection and the back-wall echo the technician is reading. Trawl gear foundations add fatigue-critical geometry that calls for magnetic particle rather than thickness measurement. Practical stations for the Alaska fleet are built on representative specimens so the technician meets that geometry in training rather than in a November yard.

faq.q: What happens if a gauging report is rejected by the attending surveyor?
faq.a: The vessel goes back for re-gauging while the dock clock runs, and in western Washington that risks losing the slot entirely. Rejections cluster around three causes: pattern coverage short of the required extent, missing original-thickness values against the measured values, and a report format the survey requirement does not accept. Agreeing the pattern and the format before the docking removes all three.

faq.q: Who issues the certificate and how long is it valid?
faq.a: The employer issues it against the employer's written practice. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the recommended recertification interval reaches five years. Under NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, which governs Bremerton-adjacent government work, the interval is three years with recertification by examination at every level including Level III. Contractors holding both scopes track two clocks, which is why cohort scheduling starts from the expiry list.

title: Working ESP Surveys: Thickness Measurement Technician Training
description: What a gauging technician must know to work an ESP survey: Z17 approval, the planning meeting, extent by survey type and age, substantial corrosion triggers.
h1: What an ESP Survey Demands of the Thickness Measurement Technician
answer: SOLAS chapter XI-1, regulation 2 makes the 2011 ESP Code (IMO resolution A.1049(27), as amended) mandatory for bulk carriers and oil tankers of 500 gross tonnage and above. Its thickness measurement is reserved for a company certified by an organisation the flag Administration recognises, using operators certified to a recognised NDT standard who can select representative positions on ship structure.
expansion: The ESP Code splits into Annex A for bulk carriers and Annex B for oil tankers, each divided again by hull form — single-side skin and double-side skin bulk carriers, double-hull and other oil tankers. A technician works to whichever branch the vessel sits in, because the required extent of gauging differs between them. Three survey types drive the workload. Annual surveys call for thickness measurement when the surveyor considers it necessary or where extensive corrosion exists. Intermediate surveys start at suspect areas for ships five to ten years old and expand to full renewal-survey extent once the ship passes ten. Renewal surveys escalate in four age bands, moving from suspect areas alone to every deck plate, every bottom plate and three transverse sections once the ship exceeds fifteen years. Substantial corrosion — wastage above 75% of allowable margins — forces extended measurement before the survey is credited.
